source: Kumar and Clark Clinical Medicine 11th Ed 2025
chapter: Chapter 24: Biliary tract and pancreatic disease

1_pathophysiology.definition: Acalculous cholecystitis is a condition characterized by chronic inflammation within the gall bladder wall in the absence of gallstones. Almost 10% of gall bladders removed for biliary symptoms show this finding.
1_pathophysiology.mechanism: The pathogenesis involves several mechanisms: (1) Chemical inflammation from reflux of pancreatic enzymes back into the biliary tree, usually through the common channel at the ampulla of Vater; (2) Bacterial infections of the gall bladder; (3) Viral infections of the gall bladder. A distinct subtype characterized by severe necroinflammation occurs in elderly critically ill patients after major trauma or surgery.
1_pathophysiology.classification: Severe necroinflammatory subtype: occurs in elderly critically ill patients after major trauma or surgery, with around 20% developing inflammatory masses with subsequent cholestasis and jaundice.

epidemiology.age_group: Elderly, critically ill patients (severe necroinflammatory subtype)
epidemiology.sex_predominance: Not specifically stated for acalculous cholecystitis

cardinal_symptoms: Cholestasis and jaundice (in around 20% of patients with inflammatory masses)

percussion: Focal tenderness over gall bladder region
auscultation: Reduced or absent bowel sounds in severe disease

atypical_presentations: Non-specific symptoms in critically ill patients
Only associated abnormal liver biochemistry may point to the diagnosis
Silent presentation with cholestasis and jaundice

4_laboratory_investigations.expected_finding: Cholestasis pattern with elevated bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase
4_laboratory_investigations.clinical_significance: Points to the diagnosis when symptoms are non-specific in critically ill patients
Supports diagnosis of acute cholecystitis; helps assess severity of sepsis
Useful for assessing disease severity and prognosis

4_laboratory_investigations.expected_finding: May identify causative organisms (E. coli, Bacteroides fragilis, Klebsiella, Enterococcus, Pseudomonas)

5_radiological_investigations.expected_finding: Evidence of diseased gall bladder wall; absence of gallstones
5_radiological_investigations.clinical_significance: Guides decision for cholecystectomy in the absence of gall bladder stones

5_radiological_investigations.expected_finding: Inflammatory masses; gall bladder wall thickening
5_radiological_investigations.clinical_significance: Defines pathology when clinical situation fails to respond to conservative management
Enables LAMS placement to drain gall bladder empyema when surgery is not feasible

6_differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_feature: Presence of gallstones in 95% of cases
Erect chest X-ray shows free gas under diaphragm
Imaging confirms fluid collection in liver
Respiratory symptoms and signs may mimic biliary disease

7_diagnostic_criteria.criteria_name: Clinical diagnosis guided by history and ultrasound findings
7_diagnostic_criteria.scoring_system: Revised Atlanta criteria (2013) / Modified Marshall scoring system for organ failure severity
criteria_list: Absence of defined gall bladder stones on imaging
Evidence of diseased gall bladder wall on ultrasound scanning
Specific features of clinical history (abdominal pain, fever, cholestasis)
Inflammatory masses with subsequent cholestasis and jaundice in critically ill patients after major trauma or surgery

primary_prevention: Aggressive management of sepsis with antibiotics
Early identification of at-risk critically ill patients after major trauma or surgery
secondary_prevention: Cholecystostomy (percutaneous gall bladder drainage) for temporizing measure in unfit patients
9_prevention.screening: Not routinely recommended; diagnosis guided by clinical features and ultrasound findings

lifestyle_modifications: Early identification of critically ill patients at risk
dietary_changes: Nil by mouth initially in acute management
10_non_pharmacological_treatment.physical_activity: Mobilization as tolerated; early mobilization after cholecystectomy
other: Cholecystostomy (percutaneous gall bladder drainage) for unfit patients

first_line.drug_name: Extended-spectrum cephalosporin (e.g., ceftriaxone) + metronidazole, OR piperacillin/tazobactam, OR imipenem/meropenem
first_line.duration: Guided by severity of sepsis and blood culture results
first_line.notes: Target organisms: E. coli, Bacteroides fragilis, Klebsiella, Enterococcus, Pseudomonas species

second_line.notes: Selection dictated by local policy and severity of associated sepsis

drugs_to_avoid.notes: Theoretical risk of exacerbating pancreatic ductal hypertension via sphincter of Oddi contraction; may worsen biliary/pancreatic pain

12_interventional_treatment.indication: Severe necroinflammation of the gall bladder in critically ill patients after major trauma or surgery
12_interventional_treatment.notes: Best option when patient is fit for surgery

12_interventional_treatment.indication: Temporizing measure for empyema in critically ill patients
12_interventional_treatment.notes: Best option for patients unfit for early surgery due to ongoing sepsis or comorbidity

12_interventional_treatment.indication: Drain gall bladder empyema when surgery is not feasible
12_interventional_treatment.notes: Stent placed between obstructed gall bladder and stomach or duodenum
